claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, staged rollout and rollback mitigate deployment risk, and the remaining enterprise refund workflow weakness can be handled through disclosure rather than exclusion or approved risk acceptance.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the model card explicitly discloses the exposed refund workflow limitation for the launch use case before certification, the verdict could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If admissible evidence shows a completed and approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed refund workflow segment before launch, the verdict could move toward compliant_with_caveats.
If neither disclosure nor approved risk acceptance exists, certification remains unsupported under the stated policy and would move toward noncompliant.
Operational readiness evidence is relevant but insufficient by itself because the governing policy turns on disclosure or approved acceptance when the affected segment remains exposed.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model card or launch disclosure showing the enterprise refund workflow limitation is explicitly documented for the named launch use case.
Provide evidence that the disclosure was included in the launch approval packet before certification.
If relying on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, provide a fully approved risk-acceptance record that specifically addresses enterprise refund workflow exposure.
Provide the materiality assessment or launch-use-case mapping showing why the refund workflow limitation is or is not material under the release policy.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a material weakness in the enterprise refund workflow segment that remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available evidence does not show that the required model-card disclosure has actually been made or approved.
The available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete: the approver line is blank and it does not address enterprise refund workflow exposure.
Rollout controls cited by the Actor do not exclude the affected use case, so they do not satisfy the policy substitute for disclosure.
unsupported_claims: That certification is currently supported on the existing admissible record without additional evidence of actual model-card disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that staged rollout, rollback, or monitoring themselves cure the model-card compliance issue for the exposed refund workflow segment.
